text:
Tyson Foerster has one of the hardest shots in the league (96th percentile by NHL Edge) and three goals to show for it in 19 games. His shooting percentage is 7.7%, about half of what his range suggests, so the goals are behind his chances. But this isn't purely bad luck: he's had 4.61 expected goals, a modest total, and the Flyers have been buried at five on five with him out there (41% of the expected goals). Five points in 19 games is a slow start for a player who scored 61 goals across his first 195 games.

The Flyers have been shuffling to wake him up, and Flying Fish Hockey wondered whether a new line might help him find his touch. Monday in Vancouver was his season in one night: six shot attempts through two periods without one on goal, then a goal that ended up not counting. He's a shooter who dumps the puck in more than he carries it, so he needs linemates who win it back. Our projection still lands near 20 goals.
